premises.text: Search is still too difficult to implement, so good search remains rare on websites
premises.evidence_span: search is still too difficult to implement

premises.text: In a typical setup the database, search index, and web server must each be changed for every index modification
premises.evidence_span: every time we wanted to modify the index, we had to change the system in three separate places

premises.text: ThriftDB combines the database, search index, and web server into a single system
premises.evidence_span: ThriftDB is just combining the database, the search index, and the web server into one system

premises.text: Because companies model their data as objects with attributes, ThriftDB is designed to handle objects natively
premises.evidence_span: So objects are so important that we designed ThriftDB to handle objects natively

premises.text: Native object handling yields fast, scalable search with attribute-level filtering right out of the box
premises.evidence_span: With ThriftDB, you get fast, scalable search right out of the box

premises.text: Schema changes require only uploading a new schema, with no downtime, cutting development time
premises.evidence_span: Now we just upload a new schema, and that's it

premises.text: The product ships as an on-demand cloud service with a free beta signup
premises.evidence_span: You can sign up for the beta. It's free

notes: The objects-world assumption and the native-object design are merged into one premise P4: the speaker binds them in a single 'so important that we designed' sentence, so the condition is coded as one design rationale; no premise-premise link is therefore needed. The three demo apps are folded into P3/P5 as demonstrations of the same capability per v1.3.2 clarification 5. D4 singleton justified: cloud delivery and free-beta pricing revise independently of the engine. '15 million parts, 300 attributes' is detail demonstrating the capability, not a separate premise. 'And that's why we built ThriftDB' is motivation, not a premise-prerequisite, so no dependency coded.
